newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds firmer, but range-trade prevails.
newsitem.headline: Bunds firmer, but range-trade prevails.

text.p: Bund futures traded quietly at higher levels on Tuesday, passing time ahead of German ecnomic data due later this week that could cast fresh light on hopes for lower short-term interest rates.
At 1447 GMT, the March DTB Bund futures contract was up 17 basis points at 103.49 after having traded in a range between 103.32 to 103.60.

Analysts said in the absence of fresh economic news, the contract will likely remain in a range between 103.10 and 103.90, at the moment appearing to lack the strength to resume its drive toward a record high of 104.04.
For the moment, the market is focused on German fourth quarter GDP data which is due out on Wednesday.

Economists polled by Reuters on Monday and Tuesday expected the economy to have contracted slightly during the quarter with forecasts for a change from the third quarter ranging from -0.3 percent to +0.2 percent.
The GDP data, however, is not seen as important as the February employment report due on Thursday. German newspapers have fanned speculation of an increase in joblessness.
The Bild newspaper said today that unemployment would rise to 4.7 million from 4.66 million a month earlier.

Speculation of weak economic growth should raise hopes of lower interest rates, helping the short-end of the yield curve. The spread between two- and 10-year maturities, however, remained steady on the day at 206 basis points.
Aside from the domestic economy, Bunds continued to benefit from speculation of a delay in European monetary union. Most leading policy-makers have sought to downplay speculation EMU will be delayed.
Bank of England governor Eddie George said in Frankfurt that in his view political determination to see the project through was very strong.
Although Bunds have gained against high-yielding markets of late, they lost slightly compared to Italian debt after Italian CPI delined to 2.4 percent from 2.6 percent.
BTPs sliced two basis points off the spread, bringing it to 187 basis points.
The spread relative to Treasuries, meanwhile, remained fairly steady at 113 basis points.
Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm could be the final word on EMU and interest rates before trade opens tomorrow as he attends a conference in Stuttgart from 1600 GMT.
